content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":3,"description_fidelity":3,"readability_1x":4,"pixel_craft":4,"palette_discipline":6,"appeal":4},"score":40,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The diagonal silhouette reads as a rocket or torpedo at 1x, not a floating squid.","The lower-left appendage is a long solid tail with scattered red blocks rather than distinct gathered or thrusting tentacles.","The large upper-right red mass overwhelms the face and further suggests flame or propulsion.","Only one eye is clearly readable; the described flashing-eyes warning feature is not established.","Black areas around the face and underside form oversized, irregular masses instead of a controlled 1-pixel Capcom outline.","The white-and-red interior breaks into stair-stepped, disconnected clusters that look noisy at true size.","The sprite uses four opaque colors across compact areas without an obvious NES sprite-layer plan.","The asymmetrical diagonal pose lacks the compact, iconic front-facing construction typical of small Mega Man aquatic enemies."],"fixes":["Rebuild the silhouette around a compact 10-12-pixel-wide rounded mantle, with two clearly separated eyes near its lower front.","Replace the lower-left tail with three or four short tentacle tips, each 2-3 pixels wide, and create separate gathered and extended animation frames.","Remove or greatly reduce the upper-right red mass so it reads as mantle shading rather than a rocket flame.","Use a continuous 1-pixel black outer contour, reserving thicker black clusters only for separation beneath the mantle and between tentacles.","Consolidate the white body into larger clean clusters and eliminate isolated red steps inside the lower appendage.","Limit each hardware sprite region to black plus two body colors and transparency; add the red eye flash through a separate palette or overlay frame.","Center the body on a more vertical axis and keep any swimming tilt slight so the squid silhouette survives at 1x.","Make both normal eyes white or pale with black pupils, then swap them to solid red in the warning frame immediately before explosion."]}
